translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 116.

title: No possible perfection can be absent from God
english: If a missing "perfection" is impossible — it is nothing, not a lack.
If it is possible — it depends on the first cause.
So it is in God at least virtute & eminenter.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 116.

title: El Shaddai — all-sufficient, not lacking
english: Most perfect: holds every excellence of every being.
Hebrew Shaddai / Dai = sufficiency.
El Shaddai: lacks nothing; self-sufficient — often rendered omnipotent.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 116; Shaddai/Dai normalized from OCR.

title: Covenant name with Abraham — God needs nothing
english: To Abraham: I am El Shaddai — all-sufficient, not needy.
Covenant for Abraham's sake — nothing God promised was lacking to God.
Creatures always need and can receive; God needs nothing, gains nothing.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 116; Gen 17 foedus.

title: Highest perfection implies infinite essence
english: Summa perfectio → infinite essence.
Nothing better than God can be or be thought.
Infinite good outranks finite good.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI PDF 116-117.

title: Creatures finite by bounded kinds — God holds every kind eminently
english: Creature essences finite: each kind stops at its own limit.
Ox / horse / man — each lacks the others' essential perfection.
God holds every being's perfection eminently — so His essence is infinite.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 117.

title: Divine perfections have no sphere or grade-limit
english: Creature perfections: bounded sphere of force.
Divine perfections: no limit at all.
Not only every perfection — every grade without limitation.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII PDF 117.

title: No superior cause to limit God — therefore unlimited
english: Finite things were limited by a cause that set their grade.
God has no superior cause to bound Him.
Therefore His nature is unlimited — infinite.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV PDF 117; next XXV+ Scriptural infinitude.

title: Scripture teaches infinite essence — Psalm 145
english: Not only philosophy — Scripture teaches divine essence is infinite.
Psalm 145: His greatness has no end / Hebrew En cheker — no searching out.
What has an end is not altogether searchable.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV PDF 117 / p. 105; Ps 145:3 En cheker normalized.

title: Infinite power and wisdom prove infinite essence
english: Scripture gives God infinite power and infinite wisdom.
Attributes = essence (simplicity) — so essence is infinite too.
Finite subject cannot hold infinite power/wisdom; what can do all things has no bound.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI PDF 117 / p. 105; tract close before Immensitate p. 106.

title: Unlimited divine perfection → God infinite in every respect
english: Divine essence has no perfection-limit.
Therefore God is infinite however you take Him.
Infinite = unbound — not shut inside limits.
translator_notes: OCR: Immensitate I PDF 118 / p. 106; Thes. Prima.

title: Infinitude chiefly as immensity (place) and eternity (time)
english: Every attribute is infinite — yet two foci stand out.
No place-bound, no time-bound: greatness without end; duration without start/end.
Prior = immensity; posterior = eternity — treat immensity first.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 118.

title: Immensus vs creatures — circumscriptive and definitive place
english: God immense: no bound of greatness; not place-defined.
Bodies: circumscriptive place (parts match space-parts).
Angels/souls: definitive place — here not elsewhere; can migrate.
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 118; Scholastic loco modes.

title: God alone is everywhere — whole everywhere, whole outside every place
english: Proper to God: ubique — not fixed to one place.
Infinite substance penetrates all; present to all.
Whole everywhere and whole outside every place.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 118.

title: Circle whose center is everywhere — Hebrew Makom
english: Wise saying: circle — center everywhere, circumference nowhere.
Hebrews called God Makom (place) — He contains places.
All things in Him more than He in all things.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 118; Makom / המקום normalized from Aktym/Makem.

title: Three modes of presence — power, presence, essence
english: Scholastics: present by power, presence, and essence.
Clearer: by operation, by cognition, by substance.
Sets up VII–IX on each mode.
translator_notes: OCR: VI PDF 118.

title: Presence by power — Acts 17 in Him we live
english: By power: He produces, preserves, governs all.
Works all in all.
Acts 17: not far — in Him we live, move, and are.
translator_notes: OCR: VII PDF 119; Acts 17:27-28.

title: Presence by cognition — all bare before His eyes
english: By presence: He sees all that is done everywhere as before Him.
Heb. 4: nothing invisible — all naked and open to His eyes.
Scholastic "praesentia" tracks cognition — like eye-survey / sun seen.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 119; Heb 4:13. Next IX essence-mode.

title: Presence by essence — whole substance intimately in every creature
english: By essence: His substance is nowhere missing.
It penetrates all — whole, by itself, intimately in each thing.
No creaturely recess lacks the whole divine essence.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 119 / p. 107.

title: Mode ineffable — not by parts; soul vestige tota in toto
english: We cannot fully grasp or word the mode of essence-in-things.
Claim only: absent from nothing; not present by parts (simplicity).
Vestige: soul whole in whole body and whole in each part.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 119.

title: First two modes undisputed — even among theists
english: Orthodox: three modes of ubiquity.
Power and cognition-presence: no dispute.
Even theist unbelievers grant no thing escapes His knowing/power.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 119; end restored from layout + sense.

title: Third mode denied — Eugubinus and Vorstius confine substance to heaven
english: Substance-presence is the contested mode.
Eugubinus: God's substance only in heaven (Ps 138/139).
Vorstius (Leiden): same — substance in heaven; earth only by power/wisdom.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 119; Vorstius/Eugubinus.

title: Two proofs — no empty place; greater than the world
english: Against Vorstius: two claims to prove.
1) No place without substantial presence.
2) God not contained by the world — surpasses it.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 119.

title: Jeremiah 23 — filling heaven and earth is substantial presence
english: Scripture: no place without real substantial presence.
Jer 23: I fill heaven and earth — not mere remote rule.
Remote seeing ≠ filling (Gaul-king / tower-watcher analogies).
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 119; Jer 23:23-24.

title: Psalm 139 — same substantial presence in heaven and on earth
english: Ps 139: no flight from God — heaven, Sheol, seas.
Not twistable to power/knowledge only without missing the aim.
Highest and lowest places: same substantial presence.

title: Isaiah 66 — heaven throne, earth footstool; same substance
english: Isa 66: heaven My throne, earth My footstool — cannot be boxed in temples.
Not Vorstius's distant-seat reading — substance fills the world.
Throne-sitter touches footstool too — earth gets the same substance.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 120 / p. 108; Isa 66:1-2. Next XVII+ immediate operation.

title: Immediate earth-operation proves substantial presence on earth
english: Immediate earth-acts prove substance on earth as in heaven.
Creation, conservation, miracles: no instruments — He acts through Himself.
Acts 17: not far away in a heavenly box outside which He is not.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 120 / p. 108; Acts 17.

title: Hypostatic union — Colossians 2 requires divine substance on earth
english: Faith: divine nature personally united to Christ's human nature.
Col 2: all fullness of deity dwells in Him bodily/substantially.
He walked earth — so divine substance was on earth, or the union breaks.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 120; Col 2:9.

title: First proof closed; Solomon — heavens of heavens cannot contain God
english: First claim closed: essence-presence everywhere.
Second: filling the universe yet not contained — surpasses it.
1 Kgs 8: heavens of heavens cannot contain You — of substance, not mere power.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 120; 1 Kgs 8:27.

title: Job 11 — higher than heaven, deeper than Sheol
english: Sophar (Job 11): higher than heaven, deeper than Sheol, longer/broader than earth/sea.
If outermost heaven boxed Him, He could not be higher than heaven.
World-enclosure blocked.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 120-121; Job 11:8-9.

title: Isaiah 40 and Psalm 145 — greatness without end
english: Isa 40: waters in a fist, heavens in a span — nations as a drop / dust / nothing.
If the finite universe boxed Him, greatness would end.
Ps 145 En cheker: greatness has no end / no searching out.

title: Could create infinite worlds — so not shut in this one
english: He made this world from nothing — could make endless others.
He would be absent from none; no reason to pick only this box.
Shut inside this world → cannot immediately create another outside it.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 121.

title: Extra mundum — God is His own place (Tertullian, Augustine, Bernard)
english: Objection: outside the world is nothing — is God in nothing?
Answer: as before creation — God needs no place; He is place to Himself.
Tertullian / Augustine / Bernard / Dionysius; possible place beyond this world.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII PDF 121; Tertullian c. Prax.; Aug. Ps 122; Bernard.

title: Heaven-habitation texts do not box substance — temple and Church parallels
english: Vorstius cites heaven-as-dwelling texts (Ps 115, 123).
Same logic would have boxed God in the Jerusalem temple.
Church/believers are God's temple — that does not confine substance to them alone.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV PDF 121 / p. 109; Ps 115:16; Ps 123:1. Next XXV+ peculiar modes.

title: Peculiar habitation — heaven as special glory and family seat
english: Ubiquitous by substance — yet peculiarly said to dwell where special glory/grace signs appear.
Heaven: clearer documents of power; earth holds sin/misery — Scripture speaks as if He were absent.
Angels and the Church's prepared seat make heaven God's peculiar house.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV PDF 121 / p. 109.

title: Jerusalem temple — symbols, commanded worship, oracles
english: Temple habitation: ark and mercy-seat as presence symbols.
Commanded worship and promised hearing of prayer there.
Sometimes living oracles and answers from that place.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI PDF 121-122 / pp. 109-110.

title: God dwells in the holy — favor, grace, John 14 mansion
english: In the holy: propitious rule, favor, grace, singular works.
Love-language: as people inhabit what they love, God inhabits the just.
John 14: We will come and make Our mansion with him.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVII PDF 122; John 14:23.

title: Highest mode — divinity in Christ hypostatically, bodily
english: Highest mode: deity in the man Christ — He is truly God.
Col 2 somatikos / bodily: beyond temple-figure presence.
Hypostatic union: divinity incarnate / incorporate in one person.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVIII PDF 122; Col 2:9 somatikos.

title: Peculiar modes do not cancel ubiquity or world-surpassing greatness
english: Singular presence in some does not block existence in all.
Still everywhere in the world — yet not contained by it.
Immensity infinitely surpasses the world.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIX PDF 122.

title: Essence through lower places does not pollute God — only sin is filth before Him
english: No fear: essence in low places does not soil God.
Spirit — untouchable by body; infinite gap — receives nothing from creatures.
Creaturely filth is relative to us; before God only sin is spiritual uncleanness.
translator_notes: OCR: XXX PDF 122.

title: Immensity implies immobility — already everywhere, needs no local motion
english: Fills all actual and possible places → immobile.
Local movers leave one place for another; ubiquity cannot.
Finite things need successive motion; immensity already has that more perfectly.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXI PDF 122.

title: Scripture ascent and descent are figurative of operations, not local change
english: Ascend / descend / approach / withdraw in Scripture.
Not local change in God.
Figurative of operations begun or ended here or there.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXII PDF 122 / p. 110; Immensitate tract close before Aeternitate.

title: Aeternum with a start but no end — life and punishment
english: Scripture often calls eternal what began but will not end.
Blessed life in Christ — eternal; judgment on the ungodly — eternal.
Matt 25:46: eternal punishment / eternal life.
translator_notes: OCR: Aeternitate I PDF 123 / p. 111; Matt 25:46.

title: Aeternum by long duration — earth, hills, Canaan
english: Sometimes eternal = very long, still able to end.
Eccl 1: earth stands forever; Deut 33: everlasting hills.
Gen 17: Canaan as everlasting possession.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 123; Eccl 1:4; Deut 33:15; Gen 17:8.

title: Aeternum for a fixed course — Passover until Christ
english: Eternal can mean: lasting through a set course.
Exod 12: everlasting Passover worship.
Bound to Mosaic rites until Christ's advent / diorthosis.
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 123; Exod 12:14; cf. Heb 9 diorthosis.

title: Aeternum for a human lifetime — Hebrew servant; Horace
english: Even a short life can host forever-language.
Exod 21: Hebrew servant forever = for life (leolam).
Horace: serve forever who cannot use a little.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 123; Exod 21:6 leolam; Horace Sat.

title: Proper eternity — no beginning, no end of duration
english: Proper sense: no beginning and no end of duration.
This is the eternity predicated of God as an attribute.
As greatness escapes place, duration escapes all times.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 123.

title: Psalms 102, 92, 90 — God remains; a thousand years as yesterday
english: Ps 102: heavens perish like a garment; God remains the same.
Ps 92 / 90: most high forever; from age to age You are God.
A thousand years before God — as yesterday; no proportion to His duration.

title: Isaiah and Apocalypse — Father of eternity; Alpha and Omega
english: Isa 9: Father of eternity; Isa 41/57: first and last; dwells in eternity.
Apoc 1: Alpha and Omega — who is, was, and is to come.
Beginning without beginning; end without end — all times embraced.

title: First Ens cannot have been made — Jehovah / l'Eternel
english: First-Ens proofs (from Deum esse) force no start of duration.
First cause cannot be made by another or by itself — contradiction either way.
Jehovah / l'Eternel names aseity and so connotes eternity.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 124; French l'Eternel; next IX+.

title: Necessary perpetual duration — incorruptible / immortal
english: Not only no start — it is impossible He ever not was.
So also necessary: perpetual duration, never an end.
1 Tim 1:17 aphthartos — incorruptible / immortal.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 124; 1 Tim 1:17.

title: Eternity proper to God alone — 1 Tim 6:16 sole immortality
english: Divine eternity is incommunicable — every creature began from nothing.
Even a supposed eternal creature could have not been; angels can still end if God wills.
1 Tim 6:16: God alone has immortality — absolute inability to perish.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 124; 1 Tim 6:16.

title: Eternal and immutable — no flux of perfection with time
english: Not only perpetual duration — the same remains; ages add/take nothing.
Creatures flux or at least take new acts/accidents.
God: no change — every perfection already in act, never was not.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 124-125.

title: Actus purus — already is whatever was or will be
english: Pure act: already is whatever was or will be.
No power to drop what He has.
No power to take on what He lacks.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 125.

title: Life of God tota simul — Plutarch's river and tree
english: God's life: not only endless — tota simul (all at once).
Time adds/takes nothing for Him; Plutarch: eternity in a unique now.
Time as river carrying the sailor; God as rooted tree the stream flows past.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 125; Plutarch Delphic EI.

title: Plato and Augustine — was / will be without change of nature
english: Plato: properly only is — yet duration embraces all times.
Was/will-be words track creaturely change; still true of God without negation.
Augustine on John: was / is / will be = never lacking, always is.
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 125; Aug. Tract. in Io. 99; Rev 1:8.

title: Malachi 3 and James 1 — I do not change; no shadow of turning
english: Mal 3: I the Lord — I do not change.
Ps 102: heavens change and perish; You are the same.
Jas 1:17: Father of lights — no change, no shadow of turning.
translator_notes: OCR: XV PDF 125; Mal 3:6; Ps 102:27; Jas 1:17.

title: Immutability from absolute simplicity
english: Reason: absolute simplicity → no change.
Change needs a remaining subject and a departing form/act — composition.
Most simple God: no other-and-other — no change can fall on Him.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 125; next XVII+ infinite perfection bars better/worse change.

title: Infinite perfection bars change for better or worse
english: Change would be better or worse — both clash with infinite perfection.
Better means a prior lack; worse means a lost perfection.
Change needs impotence or a stronger other — neither fits the first Ens.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 125.

title: No species of mutation — start/stop, accidents, quantity, place
english: Scan mutation kinds: none fit God.
No start/stop of being; no quality/accident change; no increase/decrease.
No local motion — whole everywhere.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 125-126.

title: Immutability incommunicable — creatures can be reduced to nothing
english: Immutability is God's alone — incommunicable.
Every creature depends on creating/conserving cause.
At His will, withdrawing concurrence, any creature can fall to nothing.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 126 / p. 114; Aeternitate tract close before Vita Dei.

title: Living in loose speech — living water and living fire
english: Loose speech: anything that seems self-moving is called living.
Living water / living fire vs stagnant dead water.
Flame and spring-water looked spontaneous.
translator_notes: OCR: Vita Dei I PDF 126 / p. 114; aquam vivam / ignem vivum.

title: Philosophical living — resume motion from an inward principle
english: Strict sense: can restart a motion from itself after stopping.
Not total stillness — continuous vital vigor until death.
Life = stop some act, then restart it from an inward principle.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 126; continuous vigor vs particular motions.

title: Motion here means any operation — even actus perfecti
english: Not the scholastic actus imperfecti alone.
Motion = any operation, including perfect acts.
Widens life-talk past mere locomotion.
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 126; actus imperfecti / perfecti.

title: Life’s perfection — variety of acts and self-motion
english: Two marks: richer operations + freer self-agency.
Self-motion = independence from an external mover.
More / better acts and less determination = higher life.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 126; αὐτοκινησίᾳ normalized with Latin gloss.

title: Climb toward God’s life — living bodies as divine automata
english: Approach God’s life by creature grades.
Living bodies = God’s crafted automata.
Nature’s works = divine art; human art = nature guided by mind.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 126; αὐτόματα / machines comparison.

title: Plants — vegetative life; feed, grow, generate
english: Lowest rung: plants rooted in earth.
Soul as inward mover: juices, growth, seed.
Vegetative life — nourish, grow, generate.
translator_notes: OCR: VI PDF 127 / p. 115; three vegetative faculties.

title: Animals — sensitive life and local motion
english: Animals: more organs, freer motions than plants.
Not place-fixed; vary acts by sensory impressions.
Sensitive + loco-motive faculties above vegetative life.
translator_notes: OCR: VII PDF 127; sensoria / local motion.

title: Humans — spiritual soul above animal life
english: Body like the brutes — plus a higher acting principle.
Understand, reason, know God, reflect, free mastery of acts.
Intelligent / spiritual soul above sensitive and vegetative.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 127; next IX+ human vs brute freedom.

title: Human life freer than the brutes — self-directed end
english: Humans outrank brutes by freer self-motion, not only more acts.
Brutes: nature-pushed ends; no dominion over their acts.
Man sets ends, picks means, αὐτεξούσιος — master of his acts.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 127; αὐτεξούσιος.

title: Angelic spirits live higher than humans
english: Angels: higher life than human among creatures.
Nobler intellect; not bound to matter.
Men still matter-determined in many motions like brutes.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 127; angelic immaterial substances.

title: Life belongs more properly to God than to any creature
english: Weigh life’s marks against the creature grades.
Life fits God more properly than any creature.
And in a far more eminent mode.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 127; pivot to God.

title: Creatures act only secundum quid — God from Himself absolutely
english: Top creatures self-move only secundum quid.
Acts 17 / 1 Cor 12: first mover works all in all.
God alone acts from Himself simply and absolutely.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 127-128; Acts 17; 1 Cor 12.

title: Creature freedom is precarious — God alone absolutely free
english: Creature liberty / αὐτεξούσιον is real but borrowed.
Bent under God’s supreme power — precarious dominion.
God alone absolutely free and independent in acting.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 128; αὐτεξούσιον under God.

title: Creatures limited in acts — God can do all
english: Life’s excellence also tracked by variety of operations.
Creatures capped at graded, limited action-kinds.
God’s power: not many, but all — unbounded.
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 128; infinite operandi potestas.

title: Creature life defectible — God alone has immortality
english: Even top creatures can lose life if God wills.
Relative creature immortality ≠ absolute.
1 Tim 6: God alone has immortality.
translator_notes: OCR: XV PDF 128; 1 Tim 6.

title: God alone lives simply — creature life by analogy
english: Only God lives simply and absolutely.
Creatures: life secundum quid, by participation.
Not univocal — equivocal / analogical predication.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 128; next XVII+ living God in Scripture.

title: Scripture calls God the living — against dead idols
english: Scripture’s favorite title: living / the living God.
Sets the true God against false gods.
Dead idols: no knowledge, no power to act.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 128; living God vs dead idols.

title: Swearing by God’s life — Vivit Dominus / Vivo Ego
english: Scripture-approved oaths by God’s life.
Human form: Vivit Dominus.
Divine self-accommodation: Vivo Ego.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 128; Vivit Dominus / Vivo Ego.

title: The Living as a proper title — Gen 16/17 well; Rev 4
english: Not only “lives” — titled the Living One.
Hagar’s well: Living One who sees me.
Rev 4: elders worship Him who lives forever.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 128; Gen well / Apoc 4; Beer-lahai-roi.

title: Pagans named Zeus from living — τῷ ζῆν
english: Even pagans nicknamed the top god from living.
Ζῆνα from τῷ ζῆν — to live.
Echoes the living-God theme outside Israel.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 128; Ζῆνα / τῷ ζῆν.

title: God is life itself — simplicity; fountain of life
english: God / Christ called life itself (John 14; 11).
Simplicity: God’s life = His being — no separate vital principle.
Scripture stress: fountain of life (Ps 36); John 5 life-in-Himself.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI PDF 128-129; John 14/11/5; Ps 36.

title: Frivolous scholastic question — John 1 punctuation
english: Scholastic “when are all things life in God?” — frivolous.
Bad Vulgate join: quod factum est in ipso vita erat.
Right cut: …nihil quod factum est. / In ipso vita erat.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 129; tract close; next De Scientia Dei.

title: Proofs that God is also prove He knows
english: Deum-esse proofs force a knowing first cause.
Best/wisest cause sets ends and directs creatures.
World-order displays supreme knowing power.
translator_notes: OCR: Scientia I PDF 129 / p. 117; μιμητότατον sapientia.

title: Maker of knowers must know more eminently — Ps 94
english: Creatures that know imply a knowing Maker.
Ps 94: ear/eye maker hears and sees.
Cause ≥ effect; knowing beats ignorance.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 129; Psal. 94.

title: Even Epicureans grant God knows
english: God’s name itself suggests an intelligent nature.
Even Epicureans keep divine knowing.
They deny providence, not contemplative knowledge.
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 129; Epicureans.

title: Scripture praises God’s knowledge — 1 Sam 2; Ps 147/139; Rom 11
english: 1 Sam 2:3 — God of knowledges.
Ps 147 / 139 — unnumbered, unattainable knowledge.
Rom 11 — depth of wisdom and knowledge.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 130 / p. 118; 1 Sam 2; Ps 147/139; Rom 11.

title: Plan — object, nature, scholastic divisions
english: Three questions structure the tract.
Object / extent; nature / ratio; scholastic kinds.
Limited by our mind’s weakness.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 130; treatise plan.

title: Object in general — whatever can be known; omniscient
english: 1 John 3:20 — God knows all.
Omnipotent parallel → omniscient.
Gaps in knowledge would bound and un-infinite Him.
translator_notes: OCR: VI PDF 130; 1 John 3:20; omniscius.

title: First object — God Himself; needed for creating counsel
english: Chief object of divine knowing: God Himself.
Self-knowledge is part of wisdom.
Without knowing Himself He could not plan creation.
translator_notes: OCR: VII PDF 130; self as first object.

title: God comprehends Himself — Thomas; 1 Cor 2
english: God comprehends Himself — not by bounding His essence.
Comprehend = know as far as knowable; nothing hidden (Thomas).
Creature intellects finite; 1 Cor 2: Spirit alone knows God’s depths.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 130; Thomas; 1 Cor 2:10-11; next IX+.

title: God knows all else as perfectly as Himself — Heb 4; Job 28
english: Creatures known as perfectly as God knows Himself.
Heb 4:13 — all naked and open to His eyes.
Job 28 — He surveys earth’s ends and all under heaven.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 130; Heb 4:13; Job 28; τετραχηλισμένα.

title: Not universals only — Averroes error rejected
english: Not genus-only knowledge like human sciences.
Averroes: universals yes, singulars no — false.
Reason and Scripture both reject it.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 130; Averroes.

title: Free creating cause must know its singular works
english: Each thing made by immediate free efficiency.
Counsel / will decree — not blind necessity.
A free judging cause knows its own work.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 130; free cause.

title: Ongoing rule requires individual knowledge
english: Not one-shot creation — perpetual governance.
Each directed wisely to its end.
Requires sigillatim knowledge, not only in common.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 130; sigillatim.

title: Judgment by works requires knowing deeds and thoughts
english: Final recompense by works.
Must know each person.
Words, deeds, and thoughts all known.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 130; judgment.

title: Immensity and presence — Jer 23 against hidden sins
english: Immense essence fills all places — present to each.
Near presence implies perception.
Jer 23: no hiding from the God who fills heaven and earth.
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 131 / p. 119; Jer 23.

title: If men know singulars, God more — drop from His ocean
english: Humans already know singulars.
Cannot strip that from God.
Human knowing = a drop from God’s ocean.
translator_notes: OCR: XV PDF 131; ocean drop.

title: Perfect intellect reaches every intelligible — including singulars
english: Most perfect power covers its whole object-range.
Whatever is, is intelligible — including singulars.
Singulars under divine intellect no less than universals.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 131; next XVII+ named stars / gnats.

title: God names each star — Ps 147
english: Scripture: God knows each star.
Ps 147 — counts them and names them all.
Singular stars, not genus only.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 131; Psal. 147.

title: Jerome’s absurdity — counting gnats and fleas
english: Do not spare small/vile things from His knowledge.
Jerome (Hab 1) called gnat-counting absurd.
Le Blanc will refute that limit.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 131; Hieronymus on Habakkuk.

title: Small things too — sparrows and hairs; Matt 10
english: Same create/presence arguments cover small things.
God cares for the least.
Matt 10: sparrow / numbered hairs.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 131; Matt 10:29-30.

title: Knowing the low does not soil the divine intellect
english: Knowing low objects does not degrade God.
Sun analogy: rays on mud stay clean.
Object’s baseness ≠ knower’s baseness.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 131; sun/mud.

title: Finite minds must skip small things — God’s infinity need not
english: For humans: attending to trivia crowds out weighty things.
Finite capacity forces trade-offs.
Infinite intellect: no diversion, no forgetting.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI PDF 131; finitum vs infinitum.

title: Before God nothing is properly great — Isa 40
english: Nothing properly great before self-sufficient God.
Infinite distance: our greatest ≈ our least to Him.
Isa 40: nations as a drop — else strip all knowledge.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 131; Isa 40; αὐτάρκης.

title: Conversely nothing is properly vile — glory in animalcules
english: Flip side: no creature properly vile before God.
Very good even in the least.
Animalcules display power, goodness, wisdom.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII PDF 132 / p. 120; animalcula.

title: God searches hearts — Prov 15; Jer 17; 2 Chr 6
english: Omniscience pressed on hidden hearts/counsels.
Prov 15:11; Jer 17 — searches heart and kidneys.
2 Chr 6:30 — You alone know hearts.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV PDF 132; Prov 15; Jer 17; 2 Chr 6; next XXV+.

title: By times — present, past, and future all known
english: Time-slices also fall under omniscience.
Hidden presents known.
Past escapes Him not; future seen from afar.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV PDF 132; times.

title: Past knowledge — Moses, memory, books, final judgment
english: Scripture recounts ancient past via Moses.
“Remembering” covenant/oath presupposes knowing.
Books (Ps 56/139) + final judgment seal exact past knowledge.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI PDF 132; Ps 56:9; 139:16; Eccl 12:14.

title: Future foreknowledge — prophecy; Tertullian; Isa 41
english: Prophecy floods Scripture — including Revelation.
Tertullian: as many witnesses as Prophets.
Isa 41: announce the future — mark of the living God.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVII PDF 132; Tertullian; Isa 41.

title: God knows possibles that will never be
english: Not only actual timeline — also mere possibles.
Men already know unused possibles.
Knowing His power = knowing its infinite unused reach.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVIII PDF 132; possibles.

title: God knows impossibles — cannot die or lie
english: Impossibles known too — die, deny Himself, lie.
Men already spot impossibles; God more.
Infinite intellect covers every intelligibile.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIX PDF 132; cannot lie.

title: Wrap — God knows all that can be known
english: Close: perfect distinct knowledge of every knowable.
Singulars/universals; great/small; open/hidden; good/evil.
Past/present/future; possible/impossible — if humans glimpse any, God holds all.
translator_notes: OCR: XXX PDF 132; Scientia object wrap; next Praedestinatio.

title: Roman senses of praedestinatio — glory, means, or both
english: Roman School: several senses of predestination.
Some = glory-decree only; others = means-decree only.
Most now combine both — our working sense here.
translator_notes: OCR: Praedestinatio I PDF 133 / p. 121.

title: Triple respect — act, effects, eternal relation; no cause of the act
english: Three respects: will’s act; temporal effects; eternal relation.
Of the act itself: no cause in man — unanimous.
Divine will is cause of all; has no cause.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 133; triple consideration.

title: The question — is there a motive in us for election?
english: Live question: effects + eternal relation to them.
Is there a non-effect cause/motive in us?
Why this person elect rather than another?
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 133-134; motive-in-us.

title: Adults only — infants have no election-cause in them
english: Scope: adults only.
Infants: nothing in them as election’s cause/condition.
Need a cause tied always to predestination’s effects.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 134 / p. 122; adults.

title: Opinion 1 — moral works before justifying grace
english: First opinion: pre-grace moral works as meritorious cause.
Foresaw natural free-choice goodness → congruous grace.
Named: Thomas of Argentina, Gabriel, Ockham, Javellus.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 134; Gregory of Valencia; Occam.

title: Opinion 2 — merits after grace; Thomas’s horse
english: Second opinion: post-grace merits as cause.
Foresaw right use of grace → further effects.
King/horse example — Thomas ST I q.23 a.5; Durandus.
translator_notes: OCR: VI PDF 134; Thomas q.23 a.5; Durandus.

title: Opinion 3 — Henry of Ghent / Eck; free will as sine qua non
english: Henry of Ghent: free-will side ≠ predestination’s effect.
Grace-side = effect; free-will side = sine-qua-non congruity.
Not condign merit — Eck’s Chrysopassus follows.
translator_notes: OCR: VII PDF 134; Henricus Gandavensis; Eckius Chrysopassus.

title: Opinion 4 — negative cause: no final mortal obstacle
english: Fourth opinion: negative cause only.
Foresaw: no final mortal-sin block to grace.
Catalogue via Gregory of Valencia Disp. 1 q.23 p.4.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 134; next IX rejects all four.

title: Common Roman view — absolute gratuitous decree; no meritorious cause
english: Today’s common Roman Doctors reject all four prior opinions.
Decree to all effects: absolute, merely gratuitous.
No propter-quam / sine-qua-non in the elect — Gregory lists Thomas to Lombard.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 134; Gregory de Valentia; Thomas to Lombard.

title: Vasquez — no cause, merit, or occasion in the elect
english: Vasquez Disp. 91: Catholic sentence — no cause/merit/occasion in the elect.
Covers faith-start and any honest moral work.
Excludes condign, congruous, disposition — only God’s good pleasure.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 135; Vasquez in 1am Thomae Disp. 91.

title: Petrus a S. Joseph — Quis te discernit?; Bannez circle
english: Idea Theol.: no cause in the elect for first grace.
1 Cor 4:7 — discrimination = God’s mercy alone.
Bannez, Estius, Puteanus, Eustachius agree.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 135; 1 Cor 4:7; Bannez.

title: Molina — no cause of the integral effect; agrees with Thomas
english: Molina: no cause in us for the integral effect.
Even preparation-for-grace is inside the effect (particular help).
Assents to Thomas ST I q.23 a.5 — reason only from God’s side.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 135; Molina; Thomas q.23 a.5.

title: Collective effects uncaused — but one effect may cause another
english: Collective package of effects: no cause in man.
Still: one effect can cause another effect.
New question: glory-election vs grace-decree — foresight or absolute?
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 135; collective vs glory-election.

title: Many hold glory-election absolute — grace given to merit destined glory
english: Agree: glory conferred from merits in time.
Many: eternal glory-election still absolute / beneplacitum.
Grace given so they can merit the already-destined glory.
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 135; absolute glory-election.

title: Bellarmine — predestination vs execution; per opera praevisa
english: Bellarmine: predestination ≠ execution.
Loved without foresight of works; works = path of execution.
“Through foreseen works” false of praedestinavit, true of dare.
translator_notes: OCR: XV PDF 135-136; Bellarmine De Gratia II.13.

title: Bellarmine ch. 15 — free election to glory, not only to grace
english: Bellarmine II.15 title: free election to glory too.
Targets split: predestination=means / election=glory-from-works.
Holds both gratuitous — denies works-foresight for election.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 136; Bellarmine De Gratia II.15; next XVII+.

title: Petrus a S. Joseph — glory-election before foresight of merits
english: Petrus a S. Joseph sides with Bellarmine.
Efficacious glory-election before absolute foresight of merits.
Therefore merely gratuitous — Idea Theol. I.20 Res. 1.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 136; Idea Theol. I.20.

title: Thomists and Jansenius — glory-election as free as grace-election
english: Eustachius, Bannes, Estius + recent Thomists agree.
Jansenius & disciples: glory-election no less free than grace-election.
Our conception: it precedes foresight of good works.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 136; Jansenius / Thomists.

title: End before means — glory-destination precedes merits-decree
english: Glory = end; merits = means → intention of end first.
Glory-destination precedes the grace/merits decree.
Foresight of merits follows election — cannot be its cause.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 136; finis/media order.

title: Opposite party — eternal glory-election from foreseen merits
english: Many Roman School: eternal glory-election from foreseen merits.
Not merely post praevisa — also propter praevisa.
So the glory-decree itself is not simply gratuitous.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 136; post/propter praevisa.

title: Becanus — conditional vs absolute foresight; post vs propter
english: Becanus: glory-election from foreseen merits is more probable.
Splits: conditioned vs absolute foresight.
And: post praevisa vs propter praevisa — true in all modes.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI PDF 136; Becanus Summa Theol. I.9.

title: Vasquez Disp. 89 — no free glory-election before merits; allies listed
english: Vasquez Disp. 89: no efficacious glory-election from will alone before merits.
Before merits: only common antecedent will toward all, even reprobate.
Becanus’s roll-call: Molina/Lessius/Stapleton … to Major.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 136-137; Vasquez Disp. 89; next XXIII+ Reformed.

title: Reformed unanimous — collective grace+glory predestination uncaused in man
english: All Reformed Doctors: collective grace+glory election uncaused in man.
Merely and absolutely gratuitous — free will of God alone.
No motive in the elect; only God’s beneplacitum.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII PDF 137; Reformed unanimous collective.

title: Most Reformed — glory-election absolute, before foresight of faith/works
english: Most Reformed: glory-election itself absolute, not conditioned.
Before foresight of motions, works, or faith’s start.
Grace-decree later/coordinated with glory-election (our conception).
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV PDF 137; majority Reformed absolute glory.

title: Minority Reformed — glory-decree after foresight of faith and works
english: Some Reformed: glory-decree later than faith/grace election.
God first foresees faith and works, then glory-predestination.
So eternal glory-election is from foreseen faith as condition.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV PDF 137; minority foresight party.

title: Testard Irenicum 289 — justification/glorification from foreseen faith
english: Testard Irenicum th. 289: election to justif./glorif. from foreseen faith.
Object = the believer as believer.
Time’s subordinate condition mirrors the eternal decree.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI PDF 137; Testard Irenicum 289.

title: Cappel Salmurian theses — faith-decree prior; no absolute glory first
english: Cappel (Saumur th. 30–31): faith-decree prior by nature of the thing.
First separation = faith-decree, not glory-decree.
Not: absolute glory then faith — reverse: faith then glory.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVII PDF 137; Cappel Salmurian System.

title: Common ground — collective effects uncaused; leftover dispute with ancients
english: Reformed + most Roman: no fight on collective uncaused package.
Why this one not that → only God’s mere beneplacitum.
Leftover quarrel only with older School / few Neoterics.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVIII PDF 137; common ground; next XXIX+.

title: Open question — glory-election alone from foresight of faith/works?
english: Still open in both Schools: is glory-election alone from foresight?
Some put living-faith election before absolute glory-election.
Reason named: God foresaw this one’s faith/repentance/perseverance, not that one’s.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIX PDF 137-138; open in both Schools.

title: Roman School more often suspends glory-election on foresight
english: Roman School: glory-election from foresight is the more common view.
Reformed School: only a few put living-faith foresight before glory-election.
Same thesis: many Romans teach it; few Reformed.
translator_notes: OCR: XXX PDF 138; Roman majority vs Reformed few.

title: Collective-cause question is foundational — Pelagian risk
english: Collective-cause question = foundation of Christian faith.
Cause-in-man for the whole package → Pelagianism.
Would teach grace-from-merits and natural self-discerning — condemned.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXI PDF 138; Pelagian stake.

title: Second question safer — if saving grace is wholly free and one act in God
english: Glory-vs-grace order question is different — safer if grace stays free.
Premise: nothing in man provokes the grace-helps.
And: one simple eternal will-act — not stacked real decrees in God.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXII PDF 138; conditional safety of glory-order question.

title: Remaining dispute is method of our concepts, not the thing in God
english: Given the agreed points: leftover quarrel ≠ the thing in God.
It is only how we sort our concepts of one will-act.
Execution-order vs intention/end-means order — nearly arbitrary, both blameless.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIII PDF 138; method not reipsa.

title: Either conceptual order allowed — Reformed end-first preferred; better not to fight
english: Either conceptual order is allowed: end-first or execution-first.
Reformed (and Le Blanc) prefer end/intention-first as more fitting.
Still: better neither to raise nor settle — no piety fruit, much fight.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIV PDF 138; tract close. Next: De Aeterna Hominum Electione.

title: Roman School — three senses of the word Praedestinatio
english: Roman School uses “praedestinatio” in three ways.
Glory-decree alone; means-to-glory decree alone; or both.
Eustachius a S. Paulo Summa, de Praedestinatione q.3.
translator_notes: OCR: I PDF 139; Eustachius Summa q.3.

title: First sense rarer — Biel and Occam: eternal counsel to give glory
english: Glory-only sense is the rarer acceptance.
Biel & Occam: praedestinatio = eternal counsel to give glory.
Cited via Gregory of Valencia Tom.1 Disp.1 q.23.
translator_notes: OCR: II PDF 139; Biel, Occam.

title: Most Scholastics — praedestinatio as preparation of grace
english: Most Scholastics: second sense = preparation of grace.
Distinguished from election to glory.
Becanus Summa Theol. I.19 q.2 concl.1.
translator_notes: OCR: III PDF 139; Becanus.

title: Many Romans — both grace and glory preparation in one decree
english: Many Romans fold both grace- and glory-preparation into praedestinatio.
Eternal purpose directing some into supernatural beatitude via means.
Eustachius, Petrus a S. Joseph, Valencia, Estius, &c.
translator_notes: OCR: IV PDF 139; both-decree definition.

title: Jansenius — still more general: predestination to life and to death
english: Jansenius/Augustinians: still wider sense of praedestinatio.
Covers good and evil of punishment (not of fault).
Double predestination: to life and to death — De gratia Christi IX.3.
translator_notes: OCR: V PDF 139-140; Jansenius De gratia Christi IX.3.

title: Electio likewise — glory-only vs grace-and-glory
english: Many Scholastics: electio = glory-decree; praedestinatio = means-decree.
Mendoza (Salamanca) notes the split.
Many others: electio covers grace-decree and glory-decree alike.
translator_notes: OCR: VI PDF 140; Mendoza Sect.2.

title: Effects — glory-only sense assigns only communication of glory
english: Effect-lists track the word-sense chosen.
Glory-only sense → only communication of glory as effect.
Occam & Biel refuse to count grace-gifts as effects.
translator_notes: OCR: VII PDF 140; Occam/Biel via Valencia.

title: Opposite — only means are effects; not attainment of beatitude (Durandus)
english: Opposite camp: only means-to-beatitude are effects.
Attainment of beatitude itself is not an effect.
Because praedestinatio = grace-decree only — Durandus (via Valencia).
translator_notes: OCR: VIII PDF 140; Durandus. Next: IX+ communior effectus.

title: Communior Roman view — beatitude plus means; Rom. 8 triad
english: Common Roman view: effects = beatitude + the particular means to it.
Three general effects from Rom. 8: vocation, justification, glorification.
Name covers both the glory-decree and the means-decree.
translator_notes: OCR: IX PDF 140; Rom. 8 triad.

title: Some Romans count more — permission of sins; creation (Estius)
english: Some Romans expand the effect-list far beyond the Rom. 8 triad.
Include permission of the elect’s sins — even the first sin.
Also creation & conservation of the predestined — Estius 1 Sent. d.40 §7.
translator_notes: OCR: X PDF 140; Estius 1 Sent. d.40.

title: Mendoza — predestination the first divine act; all else its effect
english: Mendoza (Salamanca Augustinian): praedestinatio = first of all divine acts.
World, creation, permission of sin — all follow from it.
Even demon/impious reprobation = effect of Christ’s and the elect’s predestination.
translator_notes: OCR: XI PDF 140; Mendoza.

title: Mendoza concl. 2 — no foreknowledge presupposed; all is medium of predestination
english: Mendoza Sect.6 concl.2: no future-foreknowledge presupposed to praedestinatio.
Everything God decrees/does/permits follows from it.
All ordered as means to Christ’s and the saints’ glory.
translator_notes: OCR: XII PDF 140; Mendoza Controv. Sect.6 concl.2.

title: Mendoza concl. 3 — no providence prior to predestination
english: Mendoza concl.3: no second providence before praedestinatio.
The one providence = predestination itself.
Everything in the universe follows from it — nothing excepted.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII PDF 140; Mendoza concl.3.

title: Therefore the whole universe is one total object of predestination
english: Corollary: whole universe = one total object of praedestinatio.
Natural/supernatural, good/evil, substance/accident, every mode.
Nothing falls outside that act.
translator_notes: OCR: XIV PDF 140-141; numeral lost at page break before XV; body = totum universum corollary.

title: Object as possible/creatable — not as fallen or already created
english: Estius/Mendoza: man-object = possible/creatable, not fallen or already made.
Because fall-permission and creation are themselves effects.
So foresight of fall/creation follows praedestinatio — Estius 1 Sent. d.40 §6.
translator_notes: OCR: XV PDF 141; Estius with Mendoza on creatable object.

title: Mendoza’s allies — Scotus: elect before this sensible world
english: Mendoza Sect.4 roll-call: Naclantus, Pighius, Galatinus, Catharinus.
Prefers Scotus above the rest.
Scotus: elect + grace-goods willed before this sensible world.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI PDF 141; Scotus via Mendoza. Next: XVII+ communior fallen object.

title: Communior Roman view — God predestined men as fallen in Adam
english: Common Roman view: God predestined men as fallen in Adam, sin-corrupted.
Salvation-decree later (our conception) than foresight of the first fall.
And later than foresight of original sin infecting the whole race.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII PDF 141; communior fallen-in-Adam.

title: Most Reformed — praedestinatio covers election and reprobation
english: Most Reformed: praedestinatio = whole providence re salvation or ruin.
Split: to life/salvation (election) vs to death/ruin (reprobation).
Zanchius, Beza, Ursinus, Perkins, Polanus, Bucanus, Dort.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII PDF 141; Dort + Reformed majority.

title: Many Reformed — praedestinatio only in the good sense (end + means)
english: Many Reformed: praedestinatio only in the good / Scriptural sense.
Acts bringing certain men to heavenly life/glory + supplying the means.
Not grace-prep alone — covers both glory-decree and grace-decree.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX PDF 141; good-sense Reformed.

title: Same sense of electio — synonymous with praedestinatio
english: Same group: electio = decree selecting some for grace now, glory later.
Electio and praedestinatio treated as synonyms.
translator_notes: OCR: XX PDF 141; electio = praedestinatio.

title: Cameronians — electio as efficacious calling and gift of living faith
english: Some: electio = efficacious calling + gift of true living faith.
Looks to grace-communication more than glory-gift.
Testard, Cappel, Amyraut, and other Cameronians.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI PDF 141; Cameronian electio.

title: Object-question opens — first party: creatable / supralapsarian
english: Reformed also split on the object of praedestinatio.
First party: object above fall and even above creation = creatable man.
Called supralapsarians — Zanchius, Beza, Gomarus, Voetius, Twisse, &c.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII PDF 141-142; Primo/supralapsarii continues past page break. Next: XXIII+ infralapsarian majority.

title: Infralapsarian majority — object is the mass corrupted by sin (Dort)
english: Most Reformed: object = mass corrupted by sin (infralapsarian).
Creation-decree and fall-permission are not parts of total praedestinatio.
Foresight of fall before mercy-election — Dort-conformable majority.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII PDF 142; Dort infralapsarian majority.

title: Some Reformed — object already called by external preaching
english: Some Reformed: object = fallen man already externally called.
Christ-sending / gospel-offer not inside the predestination decree.
Christ-mission-decree prior to efficacious leading of certain men to salvation.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV PDF 142; external-call object.

title: Sohnius — fallen and gospel-called; followed by Testard and Cameronians
english: Sohn (Heidelberg): object = race fallen and gospel-called (universal vocation).
Not simply creatable — considered as falling and called again in the Gospel.
Testard follows; Cameronians must join if consistent with their own tenets.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV PDF 142; Sohn / Testard / Cameron.

title: Creatable-object party — creation and fall-permission as effects
english: Object-view drives effect-list.
Creatable-object party: creation + fall-permission are means/effects of praedestinatio.
To life in some, to death/ruin in others — Beza, Perkins, Bucanus, Polanus.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI PDF 142; creatable → creation/fall as effects.

title: Fallen-object party — effects are saving means; Christ chief
english: Fallen-object party: creation and fall-permission are not effects.
Effects = means freeing from sin unto eternal life.
First/chief: gift and mission of Mediator Christ.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVII PDF 142; fallen-object effects.

title: Called-object party — first effect is gift of faith, not Christ’s mission
english: Called-object party: Christ’s mission/redemption not election-effects.
Those decrees precede and are presupposed by election.
First proper effect = gift of true faith in time; then other benefits.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVIII PDF 142-143; next XXIX+ comparative summary.

title: Roman and Reformed — election/praedestinatio not used the same way
english: Both communions use electio / praedestinatio — not in one shared sense.
Various acceptations in each School.
Some Roman uses Reformed refuse; some Reformed senses have no place at Rome.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIX PDF 143; comparative Roman/Reformed word-use opens.

title: Scholastic end/means split vs Reformed medium voice — election and reprobation
english: Scholastics: electio = end (glory); praedestinatio = means (grace alone).
Reformed: praedestinatio covers end and means; election seldom = glory alone.
Many Reformed: election → gift of faith (grace over glory) — not Roman custom.
Rome (except Jansenists): praedestinatio almost only in bonam partem.
Most Reformed: praedestinatio = medium voice → Election and Reprobation.
translator_notes: OCR: XXX PDF 143; Scholastic end/means vs Reformed medium voice.

title: Effects of election — same diversity in both Schools (creation/fall as effects)
english: Neither Roman nor Reformed Doctors agree among themselves on election-effects.
Nearly the same diversity of judgment on both sides.
Some Reformed and some Romans (Estius, Mendoza, Báñez ST I.23 a.2) count creation & fall-permission as effects.
Most of each School deny and reject that count.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXI PDF 143; Bannes cite OCR ‘quaest.25’ → ST I.23 (De praedestinatione).

title: Object of praedestinatio — parallel opinion-splits in both Schools
english: Effect-disputes and object-disputes travel together in both Schools.
Question: under what ratio/respect is man object to God predestining?
Nearly the same opinion-splits in Reformed and Roman Schools.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXII PDF 143; object-parallel announced.

title: Creatable-object party in both Schools; fallen-object the commoner Roman view
english: Creatable-object party: Reformed and Roman (Scotus, Pighius, Naclantus, Catharinus, Estius, Mendoza, Báñez).
For them: creation & fall-permission are effects; object = possible/creatable man.
Majority of each School rejects that party.
Fallen-object is the commoner Roman view — and the more common Reformed too.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIII PDF 143-144; creatable party named across Schools.

title: Object/effects dispute — much logomachy from unequal definitions
english: How much does the object/effects question matter? Much logomachy.
Dissenters define praedestinatio unequally — more vs fewer decrees under the word.
Creatable-object party enlarges the definition to include create-and-permit-fall.
Mendoza even draws universal providence toward praedestinatio — then creation must be an effect.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIV PDF 144; logomachy diagnosis.

title: Fallen-object definition — create/permit-fall presupposed, not inside praedestinatio
english: Fallen-object party: object = fallen sinner in divine foreknowledge.
Create-and-permit-fall decrees are presupposed prior — not inside praedestinatio.
Where definition is not shared, verbal contention is certain.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXV PDF 144; fallen-object definition.

title: Rule of use — Scripture / common Schools; creation not apt as praedestinatio-effect
english: Rule: follow Scripture’s use of the words, or at least common School use.
Schools distinguish praedestinatio from common providence (grace-gifts vs nature-goods).
Creation less apt as an effect of praedestinatio; object not simply creatable man.
Those who fold create-and-permit-fall under praedestinatio enlarge the word too much.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXVI PDF 144; next XXXVII (why some extend/restrict the word).

title: Why some restrict, others extend praedestinatio — creation not under mercy-end
english: Why restrict vs extend praedestinatio? How many providence-acts they tie to the mercy-end in election.
Agreed: acts/effects that of themselves show mercy or justice in salvation/punishment belong under election/reprobation.
Disputed: whether creation’s end is that mercy/justice end.
Extenders: create-man decree enters praedestinatio; restrictors (Le Blanc, more probable): it does not.
Creation → power, goodness, wisdom — not directly mercy/justice manifestation.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXVII PDF 144 / book p. 132; closes De Aeterna Hominum Electione.
Next tract: De Certitudine qua Fidei competit (IA PDF jumps to book p. 165; I–II pages not in consecutive PDF span).

title: Certainty in general — firm assent without doubt or fear
english: Certitudo = firmness of assent.
Mind assents without doubt or fear.
Tenacious, firm adherence to what is proposed.
translator_notes: OCR: I from 1683 Pitt (1675 IA scan lacks leaf 164); same work.

title: Subjective vs objective certainty
english: Teaching-split: subjective vs objective certainty.
Subjective = assent as it actually sits in a mind.
Objective = what the object of itself deserves / exacts from the mind.
translator_notes: OCR: II 1683 gap-fill.

title: Why the distinction matters — strong feeling, weak object (and reverse)
english: Watch the split: subjective max can meet objective near-zero.
Men often cling firmly to falsehoods or unfounded claims.
Conversely: object may deserve max certainty while assent is weak from mind’s fault.
translator_notes: OCR: III 1683 gap-fill.

title: Assent without legitimate object-ground is blind obstinacy, not true certainty
english: Mind-internal ‘certainty’ without legitimate object-ground ≠ true certitudo.
Name it obstinate, blind persuasio instead.
translator_notes: OCR: IV 1683 gap-fill.

title: True certainty needs solid object-ground and right apprehension
english: True certitudo needs solid object-foundation for the intellect.
Mind must rightly grasp that solidity — object as it is.
Sluggishness/prejudice → only light persuasion where doubt has no place.
translator_notes: OCR: V 1683 gap-fill.

title: First mover — clear perception; certainty of experience
english: Many movers of assent; first: clear object-perception.
Sense-thrust cases: see/touch → sun bright, fire hot, snow cold.
Named: certitudo experientiae.
translator_notes: OCR: VI 1683 gap-fill.

title: Mind-only clear perception — intelligentia vs scientia
english: Object to mind only (not outer sense) — still clear/distinct.
Immediate innate light → principles / per se nota = certitudo intelligentiae.
Discursive light from principles → conclusions = certitudo scientiae.
translator_notes: OCR: VII 1683 + 1675 p.165 resume mid-assensum.

title: Moral certainty from signs — letter example
english: Firm assent without demonstration of absolute impossibility.
From many signs/indices: morally can’t be otherwise (contrary not absolutely impossible).
Letter example: hand, style, contents — still possible an evil genius forged it.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII 1675 PDF 146 / book p.165; next IX fama/consensus.

title: Moral certainty from constant fame and common consent
english: Certainty from constant fame + celebrated human consensus.
Excludes fear and doubt (Rome’s consuls/emperors; Constantinople; Spain in America).
With VIII’s sign-certainty: Schools call this certitudo Moralis.
translator_notes: OCR: IX 1675 PDF 146.

title: Moral certainty is a lower grade than scientia or intelligentia
english: Moral certainty < scientia / intelligentia in grade.
Clear distinct perception + plain impossibility of contrary convicts more strongly.
Fame/signs leave absolute other-possibility open.
translator_notes: OCR: X 1675 PDF 146.

title: Moral certainty is still true-name certainty — not weak fluctuating assent
english: Moral certainty remains veri nominis certitudo.
Not weak/doubtful/fluctuating — excludes doubt and hesitation.
Authority-weight + moral evidence of signs suffice for constant intrepid assent.
translator_notes: OCR: XI 1675 PDF 146.

title: Moral persuasion enough for life — parents, princes, magistrates
english: Ordering life needs no certainty above moral.
Most life-duties presuppose only moral persuasion.
Parents/kin and princes/magistrates: moral certainty still binds conscience.
translator_notes: OCR: XII 1675 PDF 146.

title: Certainty of cognition vs certainty of adhesion
english: Moral assent can cling harder than demonstrative/experiential assent.
Scholastic split: cognition/speculation vs adhaesio.
Cognition: mind-conviction alone, object-extorted. Adhesion: also will’s effect — closer cling.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII 1675 PDF 146.

title: Measure of cognition-certainty — evidence; moral evidence still evidence
english: Cognition-certainty measured by evidence / clear perception.
Certain ↔ evident here; even moral certainty needs some evidence.
Sign/authority assent is obscure vs scientia — yet morally evident (trustworthy witnesses).
translator_notes: OCR: XIV 1675 PDF 146-147.

title: Adhesion grows with the moment of the thing — denying parents
english: Adhesion-certainty from the thing’s moment/gravity.
More tied to good/honor/advantage → stronger cling, harder to tear away.
Example: rather concede anything than deny own parents (conscience, honor).
translator_notes: OCR: XV 1675 PDF 147.

title: Divine testimony and revelation — object of faith’s certainty
english: Beyond listed movers: divine testimony / revelation.
Object of the faith whose certainty this tract disputes.
Schools + common Christian sense: highest, absolute — above scientiae; everyday ‘articles of faith’ as most-certain example.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI 1675 PDF 147; next XVII faith essence/existence.

title: Faith as essence vs existence — weak faith often lacks absolute certainty
english: Faith two ways: essence (what it can/ought to be) vs existence (as it actually is in someone).
As existent: highest absolute certainty does not always belong.
Weak faith wrestles doubt — Mark 9:24; disciples ὀλιγόπιστοι; Luke 17:5 Increase our faith.
translator_notes: OCR: XVII 1675 PDF 147; Mark 9:24; ὀλιγόπιστοι; Luke 17:5.

title: Weak faith can still be true and saving
english: Weak/infirm faith can still be true and saving.
Disciples and the lunatic’s father prayed thus — yet true faith.
Supreme absolute certainty-grade not required for saving faith.
translator_notes: OCR: XVIII 1675 PDF 147.

title: Theologians’ preached certainty is objective, not every subject’s actual grade
english: Preached faith-certainty = essence-mode (XVII’s prior).
Not subjective grade actually in this/that mind.
Objective: what faith/object by nature demands from the mind.
translator_notes: OCR: XIX 1675 PDF 147.

title: Objective summit — divine authority; formal reason is revelation
english: Objective faith-certainty = highest/absolute > scientiae.
Foundation: divine authority/truth — firmer, less able to deceive.
Formal reason of assent: divine testimony/revelation (Trinity; Christ God-man — because God said it in the Gospel).
translator_notes: OCR: XX 1675 PDF 147.

title: Two conditions for any testimony to make the mind certain
english: Naked ‘divine authority’ reason leaves scruple.
Any testimony needs two: (1) witness worthy / cannot or will not deceive; (2) testimony truly his — not fictive/supposed.
translator_notes: OCR: XXI 1675 PDF 147.

title: God’s supreme truthfulness is per se known — if perceived as God’s word, absolute certainty follows
english: Per se known: God supremely truthful — cannot lie/false-testify.
If something is certainly/evidently perceived as said by God → absolute certainty follows.
translator_notes: OCR: XXII 1675 PDF 147.

title: The hard question — how know this word is truly God’s
english: Hard question: how know this proposed word is truly God’s.
Not sense-perceived; not per se known; not mathematical demonstration.
No absolute impossibility-of-contrary as in Math conclusions.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIII 1675 PDF 147-148.

title: No infinite regress of divine testimonies — must stop somewhere
english: Cannot solve by another prior divine testimony ad infinitum.
NT can confirm OT — parts witness to parts.
Must stop in some divine testimony where the mind rests without prior other.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIV 1675 PDF 148; next XXV+ shared difficulty.

title: The difficulty presses all Christians — Protestant and Roman alike
english: Same knot presses Reformed and Roman theologians.
Scripture-alone or Rome’s unwritten revelation — both stop at a first revelation.
Question: how/by what reason we are made certain of that first.
translator_notes: OCR: XXV 1675 PDF 148.

title: Internal testimony of the Spirit — efficient cause, not a heard medium
english: Reformed and Roman: need Spirit’s secret operation — ‘internal testimony’.
Not an audible inner voice used as medium/argument.
Efficient cause of faith; still uses means/incentives that move the mind.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVI 1675 PDF 148.

title: Motives to receive the word are only moral arguments
english: Word-as-God’s not mathematically/logically demonstrable.
Motives ≤ moral arguments → only moral certainty of themselves.
Spirit-illumined ‘seeing’ still = moral evidence, not scientia-grade.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVII 1675 PDF 148; τεκμήρια.

title: Apparent collapse — faith seems only moral, below scientia
english: Apparent ruin of faith’s claimed supra-scientia certainty.
Assent because God revealed — but ‘God revealed’ only morally argued.
Seems: faith reduces to moral certainty < scientiae.
translator_notes: OCR: XXVIII 1675 PDF 148.

title: Whether ‘this is God’s word’ is an act of faith — mere logomachy
english: ‘Is this-God’s-word an act of faith?’ = λογομαχία (definition stretch).
Narrow faith-def: judgment precedes faith (else circle/regress).
Wide faith-def: two acts — word-is-divine + assent to contents.
Either way: uncertain revelation → no certain assent on its authority.
translator_notes: OCR: XXIX 1675 PDF 148-149 / 1683 fill.

title: Many theologians — Spirit imprints more certainty than the motives carry
english: Escape: faith’s whole certainty does not hang on the motives.
Spirit uses motives, but imprints more certainty than they carry.
Summit referred to internal Spirit-testimony (hidden powerful operation) — Le Blanc has followed this elsewhere.
translator_notes: OCR: XXX 1675 PDF 149.

title: Scruple — rational creature’s assent should not outrun its grounds
english: Naked Spirit-imprint story leaves a scruple.
Rational assent shouldn’t outrun its grounds (perception/signs/authority).
Else a reason-less grade — against rational creature’s genius.
Spirit works above nature, not against it.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXI 1675 PDF 149.

title: Bonaventure — faith surer than sciences by adhesion, not speculation
english: Scruple-relief: Bonaventure’s cognition vs adhesion (as XIII).
Faith > sciences by adhesion-certainty, not speculation-certainty.
Martyr-cling vs geometer who won’t die for a theorem — faith forbids lying.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXII 1675 PDF 149 / 1683; next XXXIII.

title: As speculation/cognition — faith not surer than proper scientia
english: Speculation/cognition-certainty: faith < proper scientia.
Greater cognition-certainty → farther from doubt.
Math demonstration: no momentary doubt; faith often wrestles doubt/distrust.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIII 1675 PDF 149 / 1683.

title: Shaken subjective faith can still be true — unlike defective ‘scientia’
english: Objection: only subjective faith-grade is below scientia.
Reply: tempted/wrestling faith can still be true faith.
Weak grasp of a geometric proof ≠ true scientia — scientia excludes doubt more by kind.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIV 1675/1683.

title: Cognition-certainty measured by evidence — word-of-God less clear than principles
english: Cognition-certainty measured by evidence/clear perception.
Clearer perception → farther doubt.
Theologians grant: ‘this is God’s word’ less clear than per se nota / logical conclusions — assent less certain that far.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXV 1675 PDF 150.

title: Below scientia is not yet uncertain — moral certainty still binds conscience unto death
english: Not reaching scientia/intelligentia ≠ uncertain.
Moral certainty (lower grade) still veri nominis — secure mind.
Enough for conscience-duties unto death (subject/prince; father/children).
translator_notes: OCR: XXXVI 1675 PDF 150.

title: ‘This word is God’s’ rests on moral evidence that should remove doubt
english: Word-is-divine judgment ≠ innate first-principle light.
Still founded on moral marks/arguments that make the matter evident.
Can/ought to clear all doubt in a well-affected mind.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXVII 1675 PDF 150.

title: Once persuaded the word is God’s — cling unto renouncing all rather than reject it
english: Once sure the addressed word is God’s — consider the Speaker’s gravity.
Struck into obedience: venerate, cling, adhere.
Judge: suffer anything / renounce all rather than reject the word.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXVIII 1675 PDF 150.

title: Adhesion-certainty in faith greater than in any science
english: Faith’s adhesion-certainty > any science’s.
Eagerer receive, closer embrace, firmer retain than any demonstrated light.
Rather renounce all sciences than cast off faith; hardest assent to tear away.
translator_notes: OCR: XXXIX 1675 PDF 150.

title: Faith perceives its object less clearly, yet assents more firmly
english: Object less clear than in human sciences.
Yet faith-assent firmer, stronger, deeper in the mind.
Ready to shake off any other assent first.
translator_notes: OCR: XL 1675 PDF 150; next XLI+ gravity; Spirit measure.

title: Cling-strength from gravity of the matter, not object-evidence
english: Cling-strength and tenacious adhesion: not from object-evidence.
From the matter's gravity: Spirit-lit mind sees other knowledge little aids blessed life; reject this and whole-man ruin follows.
Faith removes doubt less than demonstrative scientia — yet clings and guards more anxiously.
Maybe less by speculation-certainty; surely greater by adhesion-certainty.
translator_notes: OCR: XLI 1675 PDF 150; label XL1 in scan = XLI after XL.

title: Faith's summit certainty referred to the Spirit's inward operation — not note-measure alone
english: Whole faith-certainty not resolved into word-light or proving notes alone.
Those arguments are not the measure of its whole certainty.
Spirit stamps greater word-certainty than marks bear by themselves.
Summit cling referred to inward Spirit operation: full firm assent by a force above every argument.
translator_notes: OCR: XLII 1675 PDF 150–151 (page break mid-sentence).

title: Adhesion that beats human sciences: Spirit opens eyes and bends the will
english: Adhesion-certainty greater than human sciences: not measured by evidence; not simply by proving-force.
Spirit chiefly generates it: opens eyes to moral word-light and author-signs.
Also bends the converting mind: God's voice addresses me; stakes are the soul's whole good and eternal salvage or ruin.
Nothing worse than refuse God speaking; insane to neglect true happiness.
Efficacious resolve: receive, embrace, cling — will pulled from earth; base affections broken; Spirit's strongest work.
translator_notes: OCR: XLIII 1675 PDF 151.

title: Not by rapture or enthusiasm — yet not without object-side ground
english: Spirit's work is not rapture or enthusiasm.
Moves as befits a rational free creature — nature-agreeing.
Highest faith-firmness not wholly from object-light — yet not reasonless.
Even object-side ground: dignity and gravity the mind duly weighs (as already shown).
translator_notes: OCR: XLIV 1675 PDF 151.

title: After true faith, the word works: terror, peace, new creature
english: Another side: certainty grows after true admission of the word.
Word works hard: first sharp terror of sin and wrath.
Then sweet comfort — peace beyond understanding, unspeakable joy (Phil 4:7; 1 Pet 1:8).
Changes affections; frees from vice; renews whole man — soberly, justly, piously; new creature.
translator_notes: OCR: XLV 1675 PDF 151; 1 Petr. j.8 read as 1 Pet. 1.8.

title: Feeling God's finger in the word's work confirms it is divine
english: Word cannot so work without men feeling God's finger in themselves.
They own a divine efficacy moving the mind within.
That felt force becomes a new argument: this word is truly divine.
Paul to Thessalonica: received as God's word, which works in you who believed (1 Thess 2:13).
translator_notes: OCR: XLVI 1675 PDF 151; energiam for Greek energy (OCR garbled).

title: Experimental certainty — Spirit seals the word and sonship together
english: Faith gains an experimental certainty.
Inward Spirit-testimony seals the word in the heart — divinity and truth sanctioned.
Same witness: Spirit with our spirit testifies we are sons (Rom 8:16).
Cannot certify sonship without certifying the Father who addresses us in the Gospel.
translator_notes: OCR: XLVII 1675 PDF 151; Rom.8.i7 corrected to 8.16 (witness-with-our-spirit verse).

title: Post-faith sealing is not the earlier operation that creates faith
english: This post-faith sealing (adoption and Gospel divinity via divine effects) is not the Spirit's creating infusion.
The creating work is what people commonly call inward testimony.
Creating testimony precedes faith by nature.
Experimental sealing follows faith and presupposes it.
translator_notes: OCR: XLVIII 1675 PDF 152; illud=creating / hoc=experimental to match sense of the distinction.

title: Roman doctors split: Jansenists deny any mere sufficient grace
english: Roman doctors do not all agree on sufficient grace.
Some reject sufficient-vs-efficacious: no grace is sufficient unless efficacious.
They deny sufficient grace to all — for conversion or for avoiding sins — since efficacious grace is not given to all.
Jansenius and his disciples: this fits Augustine.
translator_notes: OCR: I 1675 PDF 212 / book p.187; 1683 check.

title: Common Roman view: God gives all sufficient grace — Scripture and inexcusability
english: Common Roman (esp. recent) view: God gives all sufficient grace for conversion and avoiding sins.
Driven by God-wills-all-saved / none-perish / all-to-repentance texts.
Else He would will salvation yet deny needed grace — incoherent.
Without universal sufficient help, the unevangelized look excusable; Scripture still calls persevering sinners inexcusable.
translator_notes: OCR: II 1675 PDF 212.

title: Recent Thomists: sufficient help to be able — but efficacious help needed to act
english: Agreement on sufficient grace for all still splits on what it means.
Recent Thomists: efficacy equals physical determination of free choice.
All get sufficient help to be able to work well — yet with it alone no one ever does.
Actual well-doing needs a further efficacious help, really distinct, not given to all.
translator_notes: OCR: III 1675 PDF 212.

title: Molina: sufficient grace enough to act if they will — use or refuse
english: Molina and most Roman schoolmen go further.
Sufficient grace not only ability — also actual working without a further prior help, if they will.
Use or refuse sits in their freedom and power.
translator_notes: OCR: IV 1675 PDF 212.

title: Roman consensus: not immediate sufficiency for salvation — faith needs Christ known
english: All Roman doctors agree: not everyone gets grace that immediately suffices for salvation.
Adults need faith in Christ.
No faith without Christ preached or otherwise made known.
Many have never even heard Christ's name.

title: Universal sufficient means mediate — more grace if well used (Cornelius)
english: Their universal sufficient grace is at least mediate, not always immediate.
Use the first measure well → God ready to give more.
Until saving knowledge of the Son — by ordinary or even extraordinary means.
Cornelius: pious with limited light → angel → Peter → Gospel.
translator_notes: OCR: VI 1675 PDF 213; Cornelius = Acts 10.

title: Not immediate power against every temptation — at least mediate via prayer
english: Likewise: not immediate sufficiency against every sin and temptation for all.
Only mediate power to avoid and overcome.
Many with present help still lose unless God adds greater help.
Yet they keep at least prayer-help to ask God for the grace then needed.
translator_notes: OCR: VII 1675 PDF 213.

title: Infants: many Romans deny sufficient grace for all — baptism barrier
english: Romans still split on further questions — first, infants.
Is sufficient saving grace given to every infant?
Many say no: many die before baptism can be given.
Without baptism they hold no infant reaches salvation — clearest in womb-deaths without parents' fault.
translator_notes: OCR: VIII 1675 PDF 213; next IX+ Vasquez on infant remedies.

title: Vasquez on infants: sufficient remedies for some, not all
english: Vasquez: the question is not whether Christ made means sufficient in themselves for every infant.
But whether He left their application in someone’s free power.
Some infants (born, or dying in the womb by parental neglect): sufficient remedies were provided — though often unused.
Others: God never granted that human diligence could apply sufficient remedies (no water; womb-death by nature alone).
translator_notes: OCR: IX 1675 PDF 213; Vasquez in 1 Thom. disp. 96.

title: Others: every infant has sufficient grace — baptism prepared for all
english: Contra Vasquez: sufficient grace is given even for every infant.
God prepared baptism for all infants, as far as in Him lies.
Parents and guardians got immediate or mediate power to baptize — and so to procure their salvation.
translator_notes: OCR: X 1675 PDF 213.

title: Tricassini: infants’ sufficient grace is in parents and friends
english: Tricassini (Capuchin): every infant has sufficient grace for salvation.
Not in themselves — they cannot receive it yet.
But in parents and parents’ friends who can bring them to baptism — and so to salvation.
translator_notes: OCR: XI 1675 PDF 213; Capuchin Tricassini.

title: How parents can bring infants to baptism — unbelieving and believing
english: How parents lead infants to baptism:
Unbelievers: grace to believe (immediate or at least mediate) → then seek baptism.
Believers: pray God keep the child to birth; baptize promptly; avoid sins that cut life short.
Mothers especially avoid what harms mother or child in the womb — then baptism and eternal salvation follow.
translator_notes: OCR: XII 1675 PDF 213; layout garbled mid-sentence — sense restored from 1683.

title: Adults: Jesuits — sufficient grace present to life’s end
english: Adult question splits even among universalists: is sufficient grace always present, or only sometimes?
Today’s Jesuits and most Roman doctors: present to every adult to life’s end.
Enough to avoid each presenting sin and temptation.
Enough also to convert and leave the state of sin.
translator_notes: OCR: XIII 1675 PDF 213–214.

title: Bellarmine: conversion-grace not always on hand — yet never denied for new sins
english: Other Romans distinguish:
Everyone gets, at some life-moment, grace enough to convert and share salvation.
But that converting grace is not always on hand — many justly lose it for sins.
Yet God never denies help to refuse new sins / resist temptation — at least mediate via prayer (Bellarmine).
translator_notes: OCR: XIV 1675 PDF 214; Bellarmine De Gratia et libero arbitrio II.

title: Some universalists: even avoid-sin grace can be withdrawn — the hardened
english: Even some universalists deny perpetual avoid-sin grace for all.
After extreme abuse, God may forsake them in punishment.
Then they are enslaved to base desires — can no longer not sin.
These are Scripture’s hardened and blinded.
translator_notes: OCR: XV 1675 PDF 214.

title: Vasquez names Tostatus, Cajetan, Fisher, Tapper for timed destitution
english: Vasquez pins this timed-destitution view on Tostatus, Cajetan, Fisher (Rochester), and Tapper.
For a set stretch of life, after worse sins, help can fail.
Not even sufficient/necessary aid to believe, repent, keep like commands, or avoid sins.
translator_notes: OCR: XVI 1675 PDF 214; next XVII+ Reformed doctors.
